title: Quinoa Casserole with Chicken
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.notes: 1 cup uncooked quinoa = 170 g (label basis 1/4 cup = 43 g); grams are the DRY weight, which is what is purchased and costed. quinoa-uncooked is a LIVE board id (2 of 7 stores, cheapest 0.1372 at Sam's Club), so this is a REUSE and not a new id. The missing piece is a vocabulary ROW for the name, which is a naming question, not a registrar one.

ingredients.source_raw: 3 Cups Cooked Chicken – skin discarded if applicable; chicken shredded or chopped
ingredients.buy: 7 cups shredded cooked chicken, about 2 lb pulled meat (2 rotisserie chickens, skin discarded)
ingredients.notes: 1 cup chopped/shredded cooked chicken = 140 g; grams are pulled meat, not bird weight. The pre-resolver flagged rotisserie-chicken as DIFFERENT FORM 'cooked', but rotisserie chicken is SOLD cooked and this line calls for cooked shredded meat with skin discarded: same form, same price class. Mapping to raw chicken-breast or thigh would be the real form flip (raw price, and a 30% cook loss on the gram weight).
Settled line; buy string derived from the table's 320 g source basis at 240 g/cup.

ingredients.source_raw: ½ small Yellow Onion – finely diced
ingredients.buy: 1/2 cup finely diced yellow onion (1 small onion)
ingredients.notes: Settled line; 82 g target at 160 g/cup chopped is one whole small onion.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 (4.5 ounce) Can Chopped Green Chiles – drained
ingredients.buy: 1 cup drained chopped green chiles (one 7 oz can plus one 4 oz can)
ingredients.notes: 4.5 oz can = 127.6 g net, about 108 g drained; the package nouns are named only because whole cans are used. The 'DIFFERENT FORM: canned' flag is spurious here - the recipe line IS a can ('1 (4.5 ounce) Can'). Chopped and diced green chiles are the same product; board carries it 6 of 7 stores.

ingredients.source_raw: ¾ Cup Roasted Corn Kernels – canned or frozen (drained if using canned)
ingredients.buy: 1 3/4 cups roasted corn kernels, thawed if frozen or drained if canned
ingredients.notes: Frozen basis 140 g/cup. Fire-roasted frozen corn is the intended product; plain corn is the acceptable substitute the source itself allows. Board ABSENT for this phrase, but a corn commodity very likely exists under another spelling (frozen-corn, canned-corn, sweet-corn) and I cannot verify the four namespaces from the table, so I refuse to propose a new id. Null gives safe pantry-static pricing while the term is hunted.

ingredients.source_raw: ¾ Cup Black Beans – drained and rinsed
ingredients.buy: 1 3/4 cups black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.notes: Drained canned basis 172 g/cup. 'Drained and rinsed' is canned usage, not dry beans, so the canned row is the same form and not a flip; board carries canned-black-beans 7 of 7 stores. Seasoned Black Beans is a different seasoned product.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 tsp EACH: Garlic Powder, Cumin, and Chili Powder
ingredients.item: Garlic Powder, Cumin, and Chili Powder
ingredients.buy: 2 1/4 teaspoons each garlic powder, ground cumin, and chili powder
ingredients.notes: Composite pantry-spice line: 1 tsp garlic powder 3.1 g + 1 tsp ground cumin 2.1 g + 1 tsp chili powder 2.6 g. Three separate pantry spices on one unsplittable line, so no single bid can carry it; the board's 'garlic' match is fresh bulb garlic, a different food, price class and gram weight from garlic powder. Null is pantry-static and safe at 8 g total.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 ½ Cups Colby Jack, Monterey Jack OR Pepper Jack Cheese – freshly shredded, divided
ingredients.buy: 3 1/2 cups freshly shredded Monterey Jack, Colby Jack or Pepper Jack cheese (14 oz), divided
ingredients.notes: Shredded cheese 113 g per cup (4 oz). Divided: about 2 1/3 cups into the mix, the rest over the top. Monterey Jack is the middle option the source names and a same-form vocabulary row; I chose the named variety over the board's generic shredded-cheese because blend pricing is a different price class (the red-onion-is-not-onions precedent).

ingredients.source_raw: 1 ¼ Cup Mozzarella Cheese – freshly shredded, divided
ingredients.buy: 2 7/8 cups freshly shredded mozzarella (about 11 1/2 oz), divided
ingredients.notes: Settled identity, but the table computed NO weight for it, so I weighed it: 1.25 cups at 113 g/cup. Divided: about 1 1/6 cups into the mix, the rest over the top.

ingredients.source_raw: Optional Garnishes: Pico de Gallo Sliced Scallions, Chopped Cilantro, Sliced Avocados or Guacamole, Sour Cream
ingredients.notes: A garnish bundle of five distinct foods with no quantity given for any of them; costing or weighing it would mean inventing every number. Excluded from the shopping list and from macros at 0 g.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS, but only just on protein, and the portions are corroborated rather than suspect.
macro_cross_check.detail: Line totals at source basis: quinoa 213 g = 784 cal / 30.0 P; chicken 420 g = 643 cal / 94.1 P; salsa verde 320 g = 107 cal; onion 35 g = 14 cal; green chiles 108 g = 18 cal; corn 105 g = 119 cal / 3.8 P; black beans 129 g = 109 cal / 6.9 P; spices 8 g = about 24 cal; jack cheese 170 g = 607 cal / 42.5 P; mozzarella 141 g = 429 cal / 33.3 P. The main-protein each-weight is the thing rule 6 exists to catch, so I checked it directly: 3 cups cooked chicken at the standard 140 g per cup is 420 g, calories land within 2.7% of the source's own figure, and the whole 13.9% protein gap is explained by the rotisserie label basis (a brined, seasoned bird reads about 22.4 g protein per 100 g against roughly 27-28 for plain roasted meat). At a plain-roast basis protein computes to 38.5 g per serving, about 6% under the source. No portion needs re-examining.
macro_cross_check.carb_flag: TOTAL carbs compute to 39.6 g per serving against the source's published 35 and this run's condition of 35 g or less. Fiber is about 22.6 g per recipe (quinoa 14.9, beans 5.0, corn 2.7), so on a NET carb basis it lands at about 35.8. Whoever runs the condition gate needs to know which basis the 35 g ceiling is measured on, because this recipe sits on the wrong side of it on total carbs and on the line on net.
